pull_request.title: Tracker: Propose reusable RD53i modules with component material accounts
pull_request.head: design/rd53-pixel-modules
pull_request.body:
## Executive summary

**Read the [three-page reviewer brief (PDF)](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/rd53-pixel-modules/docs/design/DES-001-review-summary.pdf).**

Propose reusable RD53i pixel modules in compact single-/two-chip (A1/A2) and four-chip (B4) forms. The recommendation is to qualify A1 first, then compare A2 and B4 on assembly feasibility, yield, interfaces and material. A final production family remains open.

The proposal covers the module itself, ending at its electrical termination and bare chip backs. Mounting and cooling infrastructure are excluded; the pixel volume remains open. Proposed layer thicknesses and public material data give a **0.5884% X₀ partial local reference**, not a complete module budget or area average. Missing adhesive, bump, film, wire and local-component contributions remain explicit.

Reviewers should assess assembly topology, proposed thicknesses, missing component evidence and whether the alternatives support a small reusable family. **DES-001 and ADR-007 remain DRAFT; human review is pending.**

## Detailed proposal

- [DES-001 and shared chip glossary](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/rd53-pixel-modules/docs/design/DES-001-rd53-pixel-modules.md#glossary)
- [Compact A1/A2 proposal](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/rd53-pixel-modules/docs/design/inputs/DES-001-compact-modules.md)
- [Quad B4 proposal](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/rd53-pixel-modules/docs/design/inputs/DES-001-quad-modules.md)
- [Project Coordinator comparison](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/rd53-pixel-modules/docs/design/inputs/DES-001-coordinator-review.md)
- [Reviewer brief source and reproduction](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/rd53-pixel-modules/docs/design/DES-001-review-summary.md)

Both alternatives and the Coordinator comparison were rewritten with Astra. Each proposal includes constituent thickness/material/radiation-length tables and plan-view/cross-section drawings. The study proposes 150 µm sensor silicon, 150 µm chip silicon, 50 µm total polyimide film and two 18 µm copper layers; these are design choices, not qualified hardware specifications. Material radiation lengths cite public PDG tables. Refs #7; no production geometry or reconstruction changes.

## Validation

The reviewer PDF contains three A4 pages; all pages were rendered and visually inspected, and embedded links checked. The builder enforces the three-page limit and rejects overfull layout boxes. Dashboard validation/build, 25 dashboard tests, 15 logging/documentation tests and session-record validation passed. The existing proposals' component arithmetic and SVG drawings were checked in the preceding revision. Project tracking links the new brief; exact-revision design review requests and their history remain intact.

No hardware, irradiation, thermal or detector-performance certification is claimed.

## Executive summary

**Read the [three-page reviewer brief (PDF)](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/rd53-pixel-modules/docs/design/DES-001-review-summary.pdf).**

Propose reusable RD53i pixel modules in compact single-/two-chip (A1/A2) and four-chip (B4) forms. The recommendation is to qualify A1 first, then compare A2 and B4 on assembly feasibility, yield, interfaces and material. A final production family remains open.

The proposal covers the module itself, ending at its electrical termination and bare chip backs. Mounting and cooling infrastructure are excluded; the pixel volume remains open. Proposed layer thicknesses and public material data give a **0.5884% X₀ partial local reference**, not a complete module budget or area average. Missing adhesive, bump, film, wire and local-component contributions remain explicit.

Reviewers should assess assembly topology, proposed thicknesses, missing component evidence and whether the alternatives support a small reusable family. **DES-001 and ADR-007 remain DRAFT; human review is pending.**

## Detailed proposal

- [DES-001 and shared chip glossary](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/rd53-pixel-modules/docs/design/DES-001-rd53-pixel-modules.md#glossary)
- [Compact A1/A2 proposal](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/rd53-pixel-modules/docs/design/inputs/DES-001-compact-modules.md)
- [Quad B4 proposal](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/rd53-pixel-modules/docs/design/inputs/DES-001-quad-modules.md)
- [Project Coordinator comparison](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/rd53-pixel-modules/docs/design/inputs/DES-001-coordinator-review.md)
- [Reviewer brief source and reproduction](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/rd53-pixel-modules/docs/design/DES-001-review-summary.md)

Both alternatives and the Coordinator comparison were rewritten with Astra. Each proposal includes constituent thickness/material/radiation-length tables and plan-view/cross-section drawings. The study proposes 150 µm sensor silicon, 150 µm chip silicon, 50 µm total polyimide film and two 18 µm copper layers; these are design choices, not qualified hardware specifications. Material radiation lengths cite public PDG tables. Refs #7; no production geometry or reconstruction changes.

## Validation

The reviewer PDF contains three A4 pages; all pages were rendered and visually inspected, and embedded links checked. The builder enforces the three-page limit and rejects overfull layout boxes. Dashboard validation/build, 25 dashboard tests, 15 logging/documentation tests and session-record validation passed. The existing proposals' component arithmetic and SVG drawings were checked in the preceding revision. Project tracking links the new brief; exact-revision design review requests and their history remain intact.

No hardware, irradiation, thermal or detector-performance certification is claimed.
We move this in as preliminary dsign.

While the actual module design for pixels has started in #9 we need to set up the Tracker system design as a whole:
- the envelope for the tracker is pretty much defined
- also the coverage requirement to |eta| < 4 is fixed (which one will have to evaluate with a beam spot spread at the end)
- next step is the rough placement of the sub systems and layers

The ODD should again be used as a guideline, following Pixels, Short Strips (Strixels) and Stereo-rotated outer Long Strips.
Of course, changes can be done to this, when well motivated, e.g. the inclusion of a timing-capable layer (or layers).

This needs quite some planning and inputs. The goal here is that SysArch, TrackTech, PhysVal and SoftEng work together to come up with a plan, each of them focussing and arguing for their respective area of expertise.

Here are some guidelines:
- physics performance is key (and needs to be demonstrated)
- increasingly progressinve appraoches should be used, not full-sim from the very start, a reasonable step would be 
 .  ... make some first estimates using parametric approaches (e.g. IdRes: ssh://[redacted]:7999/asalzbur/idres.git that can be used for first layer arrangements)
    ... then ACTS can be used for hermeticity studies, this can already use different field configurations, once they become available from that input
    ... full sim will require the landing of DD4Hep with Geant4 backend, this will come later 
- material budget scans:
    ... obviously this will get inputs from the module design (Pixel*, SStrip, Strip), the local support design, the cabling, cooling and readout design (only * is started)
    ... at least the machinery can be started to be tested (with some reasonable estimates at first)
- same for the magnetic field configuration.

Plan the entire process, sub-divide the task, integrate those that are already started (Pixel Module design), come up with the step-by-step approach.

Prepared [DES-005 — Whole-tracker design and staged performance programme]([redacted] with independent TrackTech, PhysVal and SoftEng contributions integrated by SysArch and cross-reviewed by all three.

The plan retains the tracker envelope and fixed **|η| < 4** requirement, while leaving internal boundaries and layer arrangements open.

| Step | Main work | Evidence needed |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Requirements and contracts | Define benchmarks, measurement conventions, beamspot and component interfaces | Agreed comparison inputs and performance criteria |
| 2. Parametric layout studies | Extract the ODD control; compare pixel, strixel and stereo-strip arrangements using IdRes or an analytic fallback | Layer tables, drawings, uncertainty scans and a shortlist |
| 3. ACTS coverage | Introduce bounded modules, inactive edges, stereo pairs and available fields | Coverage, holes and useful measurement information versus η, φ, momentum and vertex |
| 4. Material and field studies | Integrate component inventories, supports, cooling and routed services | Directional scans, accounting consistency and field-domain checks |
| 5. Fast performance | Progress from truth-associated fits to occupancy and pattern recognition; compare timing alternatives | Resolution, efficiency, fake rates, uncertainties and timing benefit |
| 6. System design review | Reconcile performance with physical interfaces and budgets | A reviewable layout recommendation and human sign-off |
| 7. Detailed validation | Land DD4hep/Geant4, integrate approved designs and compare with earlier predictions | Full geometry, material, transport and beamspot-aware performance evidence |

Material machinery, field interfaces and component dossiers start **in parallel with early layout studies**. Beamspot sensitivity enters before layout freeze and is repeated during final validation.
